name: Teach the World Foundation
mission: To revolutionize education for underserved communities around the globe by pioneering innovative solutions to enhance literacy and learning through digital technology.
theoryOfChange: Teach the World Foundation has a published 'Learning Model' and 'program strategy' that outlines their approach to achieving impact. Their mission is to use digital, game-based learning technologies to address illiteracy in the developing world. The model is implemented by 'facilitators' who provide a safe learning environment and manage technology, eliminating the need for highly trained teachers. Their approach focuses on children 'self-learning' through engaging, gamified online curriculum delivered on user-friendly devices like tablets. Research indicates that children using their model learned significantly more than those in traditional classrooms. The organization also details its 'InSchool Program' which enhances learning in existing schools by replacing traditional curricula with educational games on tablets, showing students outperforming traditional methods by 1.5 to 3 times. This comprehensive description of their activities, target population, and expected outcomes, along with evidence of impact measurement, functions as a strategic framework.

rich_narrative.summary:
Teach the World Foundation is an international educational organization founded in 2015 that deploys digital learning tools to improve literacy for children in underserved communities across <cite id="3">Pakistan, Malawi, and Bangladesh</cite>. The organization addresses global illiteracy by deploying self-learning software on tablets through its Microschools, InSchool, and AtHome Learning models. In FY2024, the foundation recorded <cite id="1">a total revenue of $363,707</cite>, reflecting flat revenue movement with a 3-year compound annual growth rate of -2.1%. The charity maintains an overall rating of <cite id="9">84.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite> and holds a <cite id="1">Gold Seal of Transparency</cite> from Candid.

From a financial management perspective, Teach the World Foundation demonstrates contrasting operational metrics. The charity maintains high fundraising efficiency, spending <cite id="9">$0.01 to $0.02 to raise every $1 in donations</cite>. However, in FY2024, its <cite id="1">program expense ratio was 78.0%</cite>. This spending level falls below the standard 75% charity benchmark and trails the median program expense ratio of <cite id="9">90.5% among global education peers</cite>. Additionally, the foundation maintains a limited liquidity buffer with <cite id="1">1.5 months of working capital in reserve</cite>.

Evaluation data demonstrates positive learning outcomes among participating students. Testing documentation highlights <cite id="5">verifiable improvements in reading and math skills</cite>, including digital literacy and student confidence in operating applications on tablets. Teach the World Foundation serves an estimated <cite id="3">25,000 beneficiaries</cite> at an average operational cost of <cite id="1">$7.10 per beneficiary</cite>. While the organization operates in Muslim-majority regions, it does not maintain formal zakat policies or zakat compliance, making its programs <cite id="7">SADAQAH-ELIGIBLE</cite> for donors.
